summary: 1936 U.S. Forest Service observation tower in Cherokee National Forest, Cocke County, Tennessee; NHLR-registered 2022. Stairs described as dilapidated; no closure or restoration found.

access.note: Register describes trail access via the 9.9-mile Stone Mountain Trail; no closure notice found in the sources read

visit.trail_note: Register: accessible via the 9.9-mile Stone Mountain Trail. Trails Offroad guide: a road leads up to the tower; stairs described as dilapidated, climbing not advised.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and the story use Halls Top; map data and the news report use Hall Top. The Register coordinates sit within about 100 m of the OSM node, so one tower is assumed.
The Register names the 9.9-mile Stone Mountain Trail as the access. The Trails Offroad guide describes a road leading up to the tower. Both are reported; the sources do not say how they fit together.

notes_for_editor: The 1936 build year rests on the Register alone. A search snippet attributed a 1934 build year to a visitor guide and said the tower had not been renovated since; I could not open that guide, and the Trails Offroad page I read gives no year. The 1934 claim is not used. The editor should check the Halls Top visitor page on theoutbound.com (not fetched) before publishing. The WATE wildfire article is undated in the cache, so the fire event is recorded with year null and the fire date should be checked; the full article text does not mention the tower. The Forest Service alerts page (fs.usda.gov/r08/cherokee/alerts) reportedly lists Forest Road 207 as unsuitable for highway vehicles, per a search snippet only, so it is not used. The HMDB marker page I fetched is about Oswald Dome, and NRIS 15000832 is English Mountain Fire Lookout Tower, a different tower; neither is used. No staffing history found. No photos added. Not verified: current stair condition, closure status, and whether the public may climb.
